messages.subject: Reporting the χ 2 statistic for goodness of fit.
parts:
hello friends, I am developing a measure for a sports psych MSc thesis and have run a CFA through R. (some of the output is below). Psych Journal papers report the χ 2 statistic and fit stats like this :  χ 2 (623) = 3175.27, p < .001, CFI = .89, NNFI = .87, SRMR = .07, RMSEA = .08. that reduce with better fit :   χ   2 (344) = 1433.98, p < .001 . My question is what is the χ 2 statistic for goodness of fit cited? Is it the model Test User Model figure or the Model Test baseline model figure or is it something else? I have read about a Minimum function test statistic...but my R output has not provided this. Any pointers would be greatly appreciated. Thank you, Tom.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Reporting the χ 2 statistic for goodness of fit.
parts: Is it the model Test User Model figure
Yes, that is your model (representing your null hypothesis about how data are generated).
or the Model Test baseline model figure

No, that is the fit of the independence model, in which covariances are fixed to zero.  It is only used to calculate the (default) incremental fit indices.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Reporting the χ 2 statistic for goodness of fit.
parts: Error variance is also presented and I am pretty sure this column is -> variances -> Std.all in the output?

As with all other parameters in summary(..., std=TRUE) output, the unstandardized estimate is the "Estimate" column (followed by its SE and significance test), and the fully standardized value is the "Std.all" column.  For residual variances, the fully standardized value is 1 - R^2.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
